ATHLET® Cervical VBR — PEEK-OPTIMA®

Modular vertebral body replacement for C3–C7 corpectomy. A base body and an end body click together (audible latch) to build the construct — 6 base heights × 3 end heights = 18 standard combinations, plus two solid one-piece units and 3 extended (special-order) base heights.

1 treatment = 1 base + 1 end bodyFootprint 13×14×15mm

Full sizing table — from the pocket guide

Implant number is what's stamped on the part & packaging — use it to pull the right pieces from the tray. Amber rows (implant numbers 14/15/16, i.e. base heights 48/54/60mm) are special-order only — no standard article number given in this guide; confirm before booking a case. Solid one-piece units (implant numbers 12/13) have no end body and no listed article number either.

ASCOT® Anterior Cervical Stabilisation

Semi-rigid titanium plate-screw system, C2–C7. 1.8mm profile with an automatic locking mechanism — self-drilling variable-angle screws lock in place as they're driven, no separate locking step.

10° variable angle1.8mm thin plate

Phase 1 — Preparation
1

Pre-operative planning

Template the optimal ATHLET® cage size using X-ray, CT or MRI.

2

Patient positioning

Supine, head slightly reclined on a radiolucent table. Position the image converter so both sagittal and frontal fluoroscopy are possible.

For the cervicothoracic transition, pulling down and fixing the arm inferiorly clears superimposed shoulder soft tissue from the lateral image.
3

Access

Anterior approach — Cloward or Smith-Robinson technique. A cervical retractor system can be used for soft-tissue retraction.

4

Corpectomy & endplate preparation

Perform corpectomy including adjacent discs, following anterior preparation. Freshen the exposed vertebral body endplates for optimal fusion.

Extracted bone can be kept for implant packing, interbody impaction and adhesion.
Avoid removing too much or all of the cortical inferior/superior plates — this can weaken the endplates and lead to implant subsidence.
Phase 2 — ATHLET® implantation
1

Distraction & trial sizing

Distract the segment with Caspar pins and pin distractors. Attach the trial instrument to the inserter and insert carefully under lateral fluoroscopy. The trial must seat firmly — if it can be withdrawn after releasing distraction, go up one height.

Trials correspond to implant height, not including the teeth.
2

Join the implant components

Read the two implant numbers required off the reference plate, then click the base and end bodies together — the mechanism audibly latches and a secured guide prevents slippage.

Check expiry date and sterile packaging integrity before opening. Compare the size marked on the implant against the trial. Never re-implant a removed implant.
3

Attach to inserter & insert

Attach the assembled cage to the inserter (AT0001) via the screw thread, turning the blue wheel. Insert into the corpectomy defect under image guidance until flush with the anterior vertebral edge — never protruding into the spinal canal.

4

Fine position adjustment

If the position needs adjusting after removing the inserter, use the positioner (GB0002).

Phase 1 — ASCOT® fixation
1

Plate length selection

Place the measuring compass (DZ-0901-B) across the area to be fused, then read the required length off the reference plate (RZ0001-A).

Keep enough distance to adjacent intact discs and centre the cranial/caudal screw-hole pairs in the vertebral bodies.
2

Pre-bending (if required)

ASCOT plates are pre-lordosed and usually need no bending. If extra contouring is needed, use the plate bending forceps (DZ-1001-A) only in the marked bending zones.

Never bend at the screw holes or bend the plate back — this weakens the plate and can compromise locking-screw fit.
3

Plate positioning

Place the plate with the holding forceps (DZ-0101-A) and confirm position under fluoroscopy. Screw fixation pins (RZ1609) into two cranial/caudal holes with the pin screwdriver (RZ0002-H + SN0004) to stop the plate slipping.

Fixation pins are single-use only — repeated use can break the fine pin tip.
4

Screw-hole preparation

Variable-angle screws: use the variable drill guide (HZ0003-H), which stops at 10° and centres screw entry. Fixed-angle screws (optional): use the fixed universal guide (HZ0019-H), 0° to the plate. Both support awl, drilling and tapping steps.

5

Awl / drill / tap

Since ASCOT locking screws are self-drilling, drilling/tapping is optional. The awl (HZ0004-H + SN0004) has a 10° stop and 7mm max depth. If drilling, use the variable depth stop (CB0086) with the drill (RZ0012-H) and tap (HZ0007-H/HZ0008-H).

6

Screw selection & placement

Colour-coded for easy ID — green = Ø4.0mm, blue = Ø4.35mm. Recommend a length penetrating two-thirds of vertebral body depth (measured below the plate, excluding the head). The screwdriver (HZ0015-H + SN0004) drives and automatically locks each screw as it seats.

7

Optional — connector/graft screw

ATM309 (to ATHLET), TM3043 (to RABEA/NUBIC/JASPIS ST) or the DC-2714/S graft screw can be placed through the plate's central slot. Slide the retaining sleeve (FZ-1202) over the screwdriver to pick up and place the screw, then pull the sleeve back for final tightening.

8

Radiographic check & closure

Confirm all screws are seated and the construct is correctly positioned, then close the wound.

Phase 2 — Revision (screws & plate)
1

Screw removal — good bone quality

Slide the ring release (HZ0017-4) onto the screwdriver (HZ0015-H + SN0004), press and hold it down on the screw, then turn anticlockwise to unscrew.

2

Screw removal — poor bone quality

If the screw can't be unscrewed for lack of bone purchase, use the 4-part revision screwdriver: thread the inner/outer parts (HZ0017-2 / HZ0017-1) together loosely (black mark visible), fit the handle and ring release, place on the screw, then turn the handle until the black mark disappears — this spreads the tip to grip and extract the screw.

3

Remove the plate

Once all screws are out, if a connector/graft screw links the plate to a cage or bone graft, remove it first, then lift the plate away.

Since the implant may have been damaged, never reinsert an implant once removed from the site.
Phase 3 — Revision (cage)
1

Remove the ASCOT plate first

Remove the connector screw linking plate to cage, then remove the plate — see the ASCOT® revision steps for the screw-removal technique.

2

Reattach the inserter & withdraw the cage

Re-access as per Preparation. Reattach the inserter to ATHLET, secure by turning the blue knurled knob with the screw thread, then remove the implant from the site.

Since the implant may have been damaged, never reinsert an implant once removed from the site.
